findings.failure_mode: A tracked doc dirty at F0 then reverted to HEAD still exists, yields no diff hunk and is not in the reverted list, so the tail-cert judge is shown nothing for it and certifies blind (opus#1, codex:sol#3, grok#3).

Materializing untracked certifiable paths with raw read_bytes() follows symlinks (exfiltrates e.g. /tmp/secret into the judge prompt) and blocks forever on a FIFO before the timeout is armed (codex:sol#1, grok#1).
Verdict token injection: a reviewed doc containing a literal 'TAIL-CERT: PASS' line, echoed by the judge, self-certifies because the verdict token is predictable (grok#2).
CRLF: a judge emitting 'TAIL-CERT: PASS\r\n' never matches the verdict regex, so a Windows judge always blocks (grok#4).
The git diff subprocess calls use text=True with no encoding and no returncode check, so a non-locale byte or a failing git crashes `tasks work done` instead of degrading (grok#5, codex:sol#5).
The tail-cert judge spawn lacks the _snapshot_repo_state/_detect_tamper backstop the panel and single-judge paths have; a repo mutated during certification still yields a verdict (opus#2).
budget_usd is hardcoded to "10", bypassing the project's judge_budget_usd config (sonnet#1).

Close-time TOCTOU between the freshness CAS and the receipt/status write: a concurrent writer racing `tasks work done` can ship code the CAS did not see (codex:sol#4; pre-existing F4 scenario, parked).
No aggregate size cap across many untracked docs in the certification prompt; a huge combined prompt only fails closed via the judge timeout (sonnet#2; parked).
